units: Milliseconds relative to the post-Google workspace navigation start; query counts are counts.
method: Three fresh Google logins using the same benchmark account and profile as November 1.
Sign out to /sign-in; select Web Inspector Console and verify focused UI is Console prompt before every command; clear localStorage and sessionStorage; verify both empty.
After workspace rendering, collect full navigation.toJSON(), every paint/mark/resource entry with timing, size, and serverTiming fields; download JSON through the confirmed console.
Match the new entry exactly; match main CSS by data-solus-stylesheet plus index-*.css and workspace JavaScript by workspace-*.js.
No Timelines recording, server log reads, code changes, build, or deployment.

cache.interpretation: Positive transfer size is browser-reported transfer; zero is consistent with cache/preload reuse. Browser cache was retained and not disabled.

coldAssessment.interpretation: HTML DB time is close to prior warm observations. Run 1 token DB is elevated and has two additional queries; cold/first-use work is an inference, not established by these measurements.

measured: HTML query count is 5 in all three runs, versus 6 in all three November 1 runs.
Median HTML application/DB time changed from 167.2/145.6 ms to 140.9/127.6 ms.
Median redirect end moved from 737 to 761 ms; HTML response start/end from 954/956 to 949/949 ms.
Median FCP moved from 1257 to 1251 ms, token start/end from 1276/1492 to 1269/1486 ms, workspace-code from 1685 to 1634 ms, host-ready from 1949 to 1736 ms.
Run 1 HTML DB was 141.5 ms, close to prior warm timings; none of the new HTML requests repeated the prior 583 ms DB observation.
Run 1 token DB was 314.7 ms with queries=5; runs 2/3 token DB were 143.8/145 ms with queries=3.
Asset cache evidence changed: new runs have 2/0/0 zero-transfer and 164/166/166 positive-transfer asset entries; prior runs had 67 zero-transfer and 97 positive-transfer entries each.
inferred: Run 1 token work appears first-use/cold-like because of higher DB time and two extra queries, but these data do not establish a cold database connection or its cause.
The lower HTML query count is consistent with the deployed schema-fold change. The three-run comparison does not isolate its causal contribution to total startup time.
FCP is effectively unchanged in this small sample. Host-ready is earlier, but cache and runtime/network differences limit attribution.
limits: Three observations per date are not controlled percentiles. Browser cache, network, and machine load were retained/uncontrolled.
The first request after deployment was not forced to be cold. This benchmark cannot establish cold-start performance.
Sign-in return paths are inherited draft routes as in the November 1 run; nav.name records each route.
Safari reports FCP but no separate first-paint entry. A workspace fetch responseEnd is not JavaScript execution completion.
Resource counts are 173/173/172, below the default 250-entry limit.
